seoTitle: How to Link Payment Processors on Squarespace: Easy Guide
metaDescription: Connect Squarespace Payments, Stripe, or PayPal to your Squarespace store by navigating from your site dashboard into Settings and the Selling and Payments sections.
intro: Before a customer can check out on a Squarespace store, a payment processor has to be connected, and that setting lives a few clicks deep inside Settings, not on the storefront editor itself. This guide follows the real navigation path: opening the correct site from your Squarespace account dashboard, working into Settings, and finding where Payments sits alongside the rest of your site's configuration. From there it covers what happens when you connect Squarespace's own native processor or Stripe, where PayPal fits and where it doesn't, and why testing a transaction before launch matters more than it seems.
prerequisites: A paid Squarespace plan with Commerce enabled — a free trial site can't accept payments
costNote: Connecting a processor itself is free. You do need at least a paid Squarespace plan (Business, Commerce, Basic, Core, Plus, or Advanced, depending on when your site was created); trial sites can't accept payments at all. Each processor also charges its own card-processing fees on top of whatever Squarespace plan you're on.

steps.heading: Open the right site from your Dashboard
steps.body: Sign in to Squarespace and land on the account Dashboard, which lists every site tied to your account as its own card, complete with a thumbnail, the live URL, and quick links for Website, Selling, and Domains. If you manage more than one site, double-check you're clicking into the correct one before touching payment settings. A processor connected to the wrong site won't help the store you meant to fix.

image.caption: The Squarespace account Dashboard, listing two sites as separate cards with quick links for Website, Selling, and Domains under each.

steps.heading: Open Settings and find the Selling category
steps.body: Inside your chosen site, open Settings from the site editor. The panel that opens groups everything into categories: Website, Domains & Email, Customer Notifications, Selling, Brand, Marketing, Third Party Tools, and more further down. Selling is the category that matters here; it's where Squarespace groups payment processors, shipping, taxes, and store policies, separate from the Website category that handles pages and design.

image.caption: The Settings panel's category list, with Selling positioned between Customer Notifications and Brand.

steps.heading: Locate Payments within the settings structure
steps.body: Payments sits as its own entry inside the Settings navigation, grouped near Customer Accounts under general email and account settings, distinct from Customer Notifications, which handles the transactional emails customers receive about their orders. It's easy to open Customer Notifications by mistake since it sits right next to Business Settings in the same panel. If you land there, back out one level and look for Payments specifically instead of trying to connect a processor from inside the notifications editor.

image.caption: The Settings sidebar showing Customer Notifications open, with Payments listed just below it under general account settings.

steps.heading: Choose a payment processor
steps.body: Inside Payments, Squarespace lists Squarespace Payments (its own native processor), Stripe, and PayPal, plus Square for U.S. sellers. Square is not a checkout-page option alongside the others: Squarespace's own documentation describes it as in-person processing through a physical Square Reader in the Squarespace app, available in the U.S. only, not a way to take card payments on your website. For online checkout, the real choice is between Squarespace Payments and Stripe as the card processor, with PayPal as an addable second option.

steps.heading: Connect Squarespace Payments or Stripe for card payments
steps.body:
Squarespace Payments is the platform's built-in processor: transactions, payouts, and disputes are managed directly from your Squarespace dashboard instead of a separate account. If your site currently uses Stripe and you switch to Squarespace Payments, Stripe is detached from the site and replaced; the Stripe account itself stays active only to finish handling existing subscriptions, and past transaction history remains in Stripe. Squarespace Payments can run alongside PayPal, but not alongside Stripe or Square at the same time.

Stripe remains available as a separate third-party option if you'd rather keep billing there. Selecting it walks you through authorizing an existing Stripe account or creating a new one, which then becomes the processor handling credit and debit cards at checkout.

steps.heading: Add PayPal, then test before launch
steps.body:
PayPal needs a PayPal Business account, not a personal one; Squarespace prompts an upgrade during setup if you only have a personal account. Once connected, customers get a "Continue with PayPal" button at checkout instead of the card form, with Venmo available on mobile in some cases. PayPal through Squarespace has real limits worth knowing before you rely on it: no recurring or installment payments, and a $10,000 cap per transaction.

After connecting your processors, enable any additional currencies your customers need and run an actual test transaction, a small real or sandbox purchase, before considering the store live. A processor that looks connected in settings can still fail silently at the actual checkout step if something in the account setup wasn't finished.

troubleshooting.problem: PayPal won't connect, or Squarespace asks to upgrade the account
troubleshooting.cause: Squarespace requires a PayPal Business account for the integration. A personal PayPal account can't be connected as-is.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to a PayPal Business account when prompted during setup, then reconnect.

troubleshooting.problem: Square doesn't appear as a checkout option, or doesn't work the way Stripe does
troubleshooting.cause: Square integrates with Squarespace for in-person payments through a physical Square Reader in the Squarespace app. It's U.S.-only and isn't a website checkout processor.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Squarespace Payments or Stripe for online card checkout. Only add Square if you also sell in person with a Reader.

troubleshooting.problem: Switching to Squarespace Payments seems to have disconnected Stripe
troubleshooting.cause: This is expected. Connecting Squarespace Payments replaces Stripe as the site's active processor and detaches the Stripe connection, though the Stripe account itself stays active to finish existing subscriptions.
troubleshooting.fix: If you need to keep Stripe as the primary processor, don't switch to Squarespace Payments, or reconnect Stripe afterward if you change your mind.

faq.question: Can I use more than one payment processor at once?
faq.answer: Yes, with limits. Stripe can run alongside PayPal and Square. Squarespace Payments can only run alongside PayPal, not alongside Stripe or Square.

faq.question: Is Square an alternative to Stripe for online checkout?
faq.answer: No. Square connects to Squarespace for in-person payments through a physical Square Reader in the Squarespace app, and only in the U.S. It doesn't process card payments on your website.

faq.question: Does PayPal require a business account?
faq.answer: Yes. Squarespace requires a PayPal Business account to connect PayPal; a personal PayPal account isn't accepted.

faq.question: What happens to Stripe if I turn on Squarespace Payments?
faq.answer: Squarespace Payments replaces Stripe as your site's processor and detaches the connection. The Stripe account stays active only to finish handling existing subscriptions.

faq.question: How do I make sure payments work before launch?
faq.answer: Run a real or sandbox test transaction through checkout after connecting a processor. A processor can appear connected in Settings and still fail during an actual purchase.

faq.question: Can PayPal handle subscription or installment payments on Squarespace?
faq.answer: No. Squarespace's PayPal integration only supports one-time payments, with a $10,000 cap per transaction. Use Squarespace Payments or Stripe for recurring billing.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded before Squarespace Payments existed as an option. Re-checked against Squarespace's official help center in September 2026, which corrected two things this guide previously got wrong: Square is in-person-only through a Square Reader in the app (U.S. only), not a website checkout option, and PayPal requires a Business account and excludes recurring payments. It also added Squarespace Payments, the platform's newer native processor, which replaces Stripe when turned on.
